candidate.blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Management of Care, printed p.7 / PDF p.11
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize required governance and documentation features of hospital standing orders.

options.A: A standing protocol developed and used by one nurse without organizational approval.
options.B: A protocol approved by the medical staff and nursing and pharmacy leadership, based on recognized evidence, periodically reviewed, and authenticated in the medical record when used.
options.C: A verbal routine that is never documented because the steps are familiar to staff.
options.D: A protocol that remains in use indefinitely without periodic review.

candidate.rationale: Federal hospital regulations permit preprinted or electronic standing orders, order sets, and protocols when they are reviewed and approved by the medical staff and nursing and pharmacy leadership, are consistent with nationally recognized evidence-based guidelines, are periodically reviewed, and are dated, timed, and authenticated in the medical record when used.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Hospitals may use standing orders only under specified approval, evidence, review, and authentication conditions.
candidate.source_document_title: 42 CFR § 482.24(c)(3), Condition of Participation: Medical record services
candidate.source_locator: §482.24(c)(3)—standing orders/order sets/protocols: approval, evidence base, periodic review, prompt authentication
candidate.stem: Which hospital standing-order process is consistent with the federal Conditions of Participation?
